name: Kaiserjägermuseum
kurzbeschreibung: The Kaiserjägermuseum on Bergisel in Innsbruck documents the storied history of Tyrol's imperial rifle regiments with arms, paintings, and banners.
preis: Adults €12.00 (combined ticket with Tirol Panorama), youth under 19 free
beschreibung:
Overview

The venerable Kaiserjägermuseum stands proudly atop the historic Bergisel hill south of downtown Innsbruck at an altitude of approximately 740 meters. Regarded as one of the oldest military museums in the world, the building opened in 1880 to honor the memory of the four regiments of the Tyrolean Imperial Rifles (Tiroler Kaiserjäger), renowned worldwide as elite forces of the Austro-Hungarian monarchy. Framed by a scenic park with mature trees, the museum combines military history exhibits with breathtaking vistas across Innsbruck, the Inn Valley, and the dramatic Nordkette limestone range. Its storied historic location on this memorial hilltop establishes the site as a profound landmark of Tyrolean identity.

Route & Requirements

Today, the museum is directly linked underground to the contemporary Tirol Panorama exhibition complex. The extensive collection displays authentic uniforms, battle flags, medals, oil paintings, weapons, and personal gear belonging to Tyrolean riflemen from the 19th and early 20th centuries. A major focus is dedicated to the military campaigns of the Kaiserjäger, high-alpine combat along the Dolomite and Isonzo fronts in World War I, and the close historic ties between the corps and the House of Habsburg. Highlights include the Regimental Banner Hall showcasing historic standard ribbons and portraits of famed commanders. Historical maps, terrain relief models, and mountain warfare equipment illustrate the extreme challenges of high-alpine combat in ice and rock. Touching personal letters, diaries, and field photographs provide human insight into wartime mountain hardships. Outside, the Andreas Hofer memorial commemorates the 1809 battles of Bergisel.

Visit & Arrival

The museum is open year-round from Wednesday to Monday between 09:00 and 17:00 (closed Tuesdays). Admission is included with the Tirol Panorama ticket (€12.00 adults, €9.00 concessions, youth under 19 free; free with the Innsbruck Card). By transit: take tram line 1 or 6 from Innsbruck city center to the Bergisel stop, then walk five minutes along a signposted panoramic path to the entrance. By car: Brenner autobahn A13 (exit Innsbruck-Süd) or A12 (exit Innsbruck-Mitte); parking is provided on Bergisel.

Tips

Thanks to the modern connecting wing to the Tirol Panorama, the museum is barrier-free and fully accessible by elevators. Be sure to admire the monumental 1,000-square-meter panoramic painting and relax on the panoramic terrace of the restaurant overlooking the world-famous Bergisel ski jump. Enjoy a peaceful circular walk along the wooded Bergisel trails following your museum tour.
